interpretations.decision: The read-only query server reads only the current generation (graph.9.db). Current is always a GC root and GC never touches the live store (graph.9.db, source-snapshots/), which the inline snap.retain still owns; in-flight server readers are additionally FD-pinned (snapshots.py:3-4). Cross-process flock leases protect retained non-current generations accessed through storage.leases.acquire and 'atlas-aci jobs acquire'. server.py, query/*, protocol/* and config.py stay byte-identical. Wiring serve to non-current generations is a documented follow-up

The build runs in the 'atlas-aci jobs submit|resume' command process via indexing/job_runner.run_from_cli, not in a spawned child, because a new subprocess.Popen site would break test_s40_injection.py:371-375. Process isolation, SIGKILL and SIGTERM semantics are identical; ATLAS_ACI_JOB_FAULTS is read only in run_from_cli

Checkpoints are content-addressed extraction-cache entries recorded in an append-only fsynced checkpoint.log with a chained digest, plus a constant-size checkpoint.json summary (fsync+rename). Resume re-runs; cache hits prove continuation (parser_invocations == files - valid prefix)

Same-filesystem hardlink farm <atlas_dir>/generations/<generation_id>/ (graph.9.db, source-snapshots manifest+pack, lease.lock, meta.json), captured under the writer lock (inside the build's own critical section for jobs; at GC start for unmanaged publishers). Cross-device is refused with CROSS_DEVICE. Verification repeats reader_lease's validation on the farm through a repo-bound read-only CodeGraph (private coupling listed, parity-tested)

Identical job identity with a receipt whose generation passes a full lease acquisition, digest verification and identity binding returns the stored receipt with no work. Missing, retired, raced, digest-invalid or identity-mismatched output declines with a closed reason and re-runs. Re-publishing a retained output as current is out of scope
